stories.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Latvia
stories.summary: Jets have shot down a foreign drone over Latvia after it entered the Baltic state's airspace. Its origin remains unclear, but the incident adds to concern over repeated incursions along NATO's eastern flank.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IofK The Italian Eurofighter was scrambled from a base in neighboring Lithuania Image: GIUSEPPE LAMI/ANSA/picture alliance Advertisement NATO fighter jets have shot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the alliance and Latvian authorities said Friday. Two Italian Eurofighters were scrambled and one destroyed the unmanned aircraft, while two Turkish F-16s were also deployed under NATO command. What happened over Latvia? Latvia's military initially issued an air alert and urged people in affected areas to remain indoors and seek shelter. Authorities said the foreign drone entered Latvian airspace over the Balvi region as a result of Russian electronic warfare activity. It was not immediately clear where the drone originated, and NATO said an investigation was underway. Latvian authorities did not identify the drone as Ukrainian. However, the reference to Russian electronic warfare raised the possibility that a Ukrainian drone targeting Russia had been forced off course by interference. stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, Hannibal Hanschke/EPA/Shutterstock Image caption, The 71st Eurovision final will take place on 15 May 2027 in Burgos, Bulgaria after singer Dara's win last time out By Paul Glynn Culture reporter Published 1 hour ago Eurovision 2027 will be a seaside song contest held in the Bulgarian city of Burgas, organisers have confirmed. The competition will take place in the city, which is close to the Black Sea, from 12 to 15 May, the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) and Bulgarian National Television (BNT) announced on Thursday. It comes after Bulgarian singer Dara won this year's contest in Vienna, Austria in May - her country's first Eurovision win - with her pneumatic dance anthem Bangaranga. stories.summary: The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia's largest disaster responses in years.

stories.title: Trump hails 'wall of steel' blockade, says US will keep control of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran maintains it effectively controls much of the waterway and intends to impose a toll system in response to the US war launched by Trump on 28 February.

stories.title: Australia's game-changing disability support is in crisis – what went wrong?
stories.summary: The programme was game-changing for its users - but as costs balloon, its success has led to its downfall.

stories.title: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave role at end of month, Trump says
stories.summary: Leavitt's departure comes as Trump faces steadily sinking poll numbers and the Republican Party risks defeat in the November midterm elections.

stories.title: Why are 'human fridges' being sold in Japan?
stories.summary: As Japan swelters through extreme summer heat, BBC Tokyo correspondent Kurumi Mori tries out a new way to cool down.

stories.title: Vultures are disappearing in Nigeria - but the 'Vulture King' is fighting to reverse the trend
stories.summary: Some see them as sinister or hunt them for ritual use but these birds play a vital role in nature's cycle.

stories.title: Travis Kelce shares first details from his wedding to Taylor Swift: 'Best night of my life'
stories.summary: In the comments, Kelce called Swift his "wife" for first time and said it was a "childhood dream" to wed at Madison Square Garden.

stories.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak on track to surpass deadliest in history, WHO chief says
stories.summary: “At its current pace, it’s on track to eclipse the West African Ebola outbreak of 2014 to 2016,” WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told reporters on Wednesday.

stories.title: Rare eclipse plunges parts of Europe into darkness
stories.summary: Skywatchers across Europe gathered to watch a rare solar eclipse, using protective glasses as the Moon passed in front of the Sun.

stories.title: Half a million visitors flock to Spain’s path of total solar eclipse
stories.summary: Spain witnessed its first total solar eclipse in more than a century on Wednesday 12 August, drawing millions of people to viewing sites across the north of the country as the Moon passed directly in front of the Sun.

stories.title: Colombia: "scene of horror" as Pereira rescuers search rubble
stories.summary: Colombia's earthquake death toll rose to 265 in Pereira by 12 August 2026, with almost 500 still missing. Rescuers described scenes of horror as the critical 72-hour survival window closed.

stories.title: Timelapse of partial solar eclipse seen from Royal Observatory Greenwich
stories.summary: Britain witnessed its most significant solar eclipse since 1999, with more than 90% of the Sun obscured in some parts of the country. Crowds gathered in parks and open spaces to watch the rare celestial event. In London, the sky turned an eerie grey as a sliver of sunlight appeared above the Moon.

stories.title: Soaring stingray numbers off California beaches drive record injuries
stories.summary: California is seeing unusually large numbers of round stingrays near its beaches, as warmer coastal waters and an expected strong El Niño draw the animals closer to shore.

stories.title: France accues Iran of 'bloodshed' over use of death penalty
stories.summary: After a statement condemning Iran's use of the death penalty, tensions rose between senior diplomats. Paris accused Tehran of 'bloodshed' and Iran called France's stance 'blatant hypocrisy.'
